The focal object is the smallest compatible Gaussian common radius \(r_\alpha(F,p)\) for a DIM-centered confidence square. Eight fixed quadratic transport costs and six exposed covariance-edge directions provide a proposed structural reduction, with a constant-trace facet retained through its zero-covariance section. Observed arm-vector frequencies then yield uniform design-based coverage and first-order smallest common radius within the continuous deterministic limiting-radius class.
